name: Daily AI Toll
topics: the history of AI, its models and milestones, its economics, and how its cost to working people is measured

questions.q: In which journal did Alan Turing publish "Computing Machinery and Intelligence" in 1950?
questions.explain: Turing's paper appeared in the philosophy journal Mind in 1950. It proposed a test of machine intelligence that is now known as the Turing test.
questions.source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, The Turing Test, https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/turing-test/

questions.q: What name did Turing himself give to the test now called the Turing test?
questions.explain: Turing called his proposal the imitation game. An interrogator questions two unseen participants and tries to tell which one is the machine.
questions.source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, The Turing Test, https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/turing-test/

questions.q: Turing predicted that by about the year 2000 an average interrogator would have no more than what chance of a correct identification after five minutes of questioning?
questions.explain: Turing wrote that an average interrogator would not have more than a 70 percent chance of making the right identification after five minutes. No machine met this benchmark by 2000.
questions.source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, The Turing Test, https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/turing-test/

questions.q: In what year was the Dartmouth summer research project on artificial intelligence held?
questions.explain: The proposal, dated August 31, 1955, called for a study during the summer of 1956 at Dartmouth College in Hanover, New Hampshire.
questions.source: Stanford University (John McCarthy), A Proposal for the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence, https://www-formal.stanford.edu/jmc/history/dartmouth/dartmouth.html

questions.q: Which of these people was NOT one of the four authors of the 1955 Dartmouth AI proposal?
questions.explain: The proposal was signed by John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, Nathaniel Rochester and Claude Shannon. Turing was not an author.
questions.source: Stanford University (John McCarthy), A Proposal for the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence, https://www-formal.stanford.edu/jmc/history/dartmouth/dartmouth.html

questions.q: How large a study did the 1955 Dartmouth proposal ask for?
questions.explain: The proposal requested "a 2 month, 10 man study of artificial intelligence" during the summer of 1956. It was written by McCarthy, Minsky, Rochester and Shannon.
questions.source: Stanford University (John McCarthy), A Proposal for the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence, https://www-formal.stanford.edu/jmc/history/dartmouth/dartmouth.html

questions.q: Which organization funded Frank Rosenblatt's perceptron work, demonstrated in July 1958?
options: The U.S. Office of Naval Research
questions.explain: The perceptron was funded by the U.S. Office of Naval Research. The New York Times described it as a "new Navy device" that learns by doing.
questions.source: Cornell Chronicle, Professor's perceptron paved the way for AI, 60 years too soon, https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2019/09/professors-perceptron-paved-way-ai-60-years-too-soon

questions.q: In the 1958 perceptron demonstration, which computer taught itself to tell left-marked punch cards from right-marked ones?
questions.explain: An IBM 704 was fed punch cards and after 50 trials learned to distinguish cards marked on the left from cards marked on the right.
questions.source: Cornell Chronicle, Professor's perceptron paved the way for AI, 60 years too soon, https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2019/09/professors-perceptron-paved-way-ai-60-years-too-soon

questions.q: Who created the ELIZA chatbot at MIT in the mid 1960s?
questions.explain: Joseph Weizenbaum wrote ELIZA at MIT between 1964 and 1967. His paper on it appeared in Communications of the ACM in January 1966.
questions.source: Wikipedia, ELIZA, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ELIZA

questions.q: ELIZA's best known script, DOCTOR, imitated which style of psychotherapy?
questions.explain: The DOCTOR script imitated a Rogerian therapist, who reflects the patient's statements back. Weizenbaum was surprised that his own secretary wanted privacy to talk with it.
questions.source: Wikipedia, ELIZA, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ELIZA

questions.q: In what year was the Lighthill report on artificial intelligence published in the United Kingdom?
questions.explain: James Lighthill's report, "Artificial Intelligence: A General Survey," was published in 1973. It led the British government to withdraw support for AI research at most British universities.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Lighthill report, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighthill_report

questions.q: Which body commissioned the Lighthill report on AI in 1972?
questions.explain: The British Science Research Council commissioned Lighthill in 1972 to review the field. His pessimistic findings contributed to an AI winter in the UK.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Lighthill report, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighthill_report

questions.q: The first major AI winter is usually dated to approximately which span of years?
questions.explain: The two major AI winters are usually dated to approximately 1974 to 1980 and 1987 to 2000. Both followed periods of high expectations and cuts in funding.
questions.source: Wikipedia, AI winter, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_winter

questions.q: The 1966 ALPAC report, an early blow to AI funding, judged which technology to be slower, less accurate and more expensive than people?
questions.explain: The ALPAC report concluded that machine translation was more expensive, less accurate and slower than human translation.
questions.source: Wikipedia, AI winter, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_winter

questions.q: Who wrote the 1969 book "Perceptrons," which set out the limits of single-layer networks?
questions.explain: Marvin Minsky and Seymour Papert published "Perceptrons" through MIT Press in 1969. It showed functions such as XOR that a single-layer perceptron cannot compute.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Perceptrons (book), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perceptrons_(book)

questions.q: Arthur Samuel, who coined the term "machine learning" in 1959, is known for a program that played which game?
questions.explain: Samuel's 1959 paper was titled "Some Studies in Machine Learning Using the Game of Checkers." He built the program at IBM.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Arthur Samuel (computer scientist), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Samuel_(computer_scientist)

questions.q: Who designed the Lisp programming language, beginning in 1958?
questions.explain: John McCarthy began developing Lisp at MIT in 1958 and published its design in Communications of the ACM in April 1960. The name comes from "List Processor."
questions.source: Wikipedia, Lisp (programming language), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisp_(programming_language)

questions.q: Lisp is described as the second-oldest high-level programming language still in common use. Which language is older?
questions.explain: Only Fortran is older among high-level languages still in common use.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Lisp (programming language), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisp_(programming_language)

questions.q: The 1970s expert system MYCIN was built at Stanford to do what?
options: Identify bacteria in severe infections and recommend antibiotics
questions.explain: MYCIN identified bacteria causing infections such as bacteremia and meningitis and recommended antibiotics with doses adjusted for body weight. It was written in Lisp as Edward Shortliffe's doctoral work.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Mycin, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mycin

questions.q: About how many production rules did the MYCIN expert system use?
questions.explain: MYCIN worked from a knowledge base of approximately 600 rules. It used backward chaining to rank likely bacteria and suggest treatment.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Mycin, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mycin

questions.q: Which company used the XCON expert system to configure its VAX computer orders?
questions.explain: XCON was developed by John McDermott of Carnegie Mellon for Digital Equipment Corporation and first deployed in 1980. It selected components for VAX systems to match customer orders.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Xcon, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xcon

questions.q: By 1986, how much was the XCON expert system estimated to save Digital Equipment Corporation each year?
questions.explain: By 1986 XCON was estimated to be saving DEC $25 million a year. It had processed 80,000 orders by that point.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Xcon, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xcon

questions.q: Which country launched the Fifth Generation Computer Systems project in 1982?
questions.explain: Japan's Ministry of International Trade and Industry launched the project in 1982. It aimed at massively parallel computers for AI and spent about 57 billion yen.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Fifth Generation Computer Systems, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_Generation_Computer_Systems

questions.q: Japan's Fifth Generation Computer Systems project was built around which programming approach?
questions.explain: The project chose logic programming, centered on Prolog and concurrent logic languages. Conventional hardware from firms such as Sun and Intel later outperformed its specialized machines.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Fifth Generation Computer Systems, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_Generation_Computer_Systems

questions.q: In which journal did Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams publish their 1986 paper that popularized backpropagation?
questions.explain: The 1986 paper by David Rumelhart, Geoffrey Hinton and Ronald Williams appeared in Nature. It popularized backpropagation for training multilayer networks.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Geoffrey Hinton, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoffrey_Hinton

questions.q: Who introduced the long short-term memory (LSTM) network in 1997?
questions.explain: Sepp Hochreiter and Jurgen Schmidhuber introduced LSTM in Neural Computation in 1997. It was designed to address the vanishing gradient problem in recurrent networks.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Long short-term memory, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_short-term_memory

questions.q: Yann LeCun's group developed the LeNet convolutional networks at which laboratory?
questions.explain: LeNet was created at AT&T Bell Laboratories in Holmdel, New Jersey, starting in 1988. The 1989 version read handwritten zip codes from the US Postal Service.
questions.source: Wikipedia, LeNet, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeNet

questions.q: As of 2001, the check-reading system based on LeNet processed about what share of all checks in the US?
questions.explain: As of 2001 the system processed about 20 million checks a day, or 10 percent of all checks in the US. NCR had deployed it in bank back offices from 1996.
questions.source: Wikipedia, LeNet, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeNet

questions.q: What was the final score when IBM's Deep Blue beat Garry Kasparov in their May 1997 rematch?
questions.explain: Deep Blue won the 1997 rematch in New York 3.5 to 2.5, winning two games with three draws. It was the first time a computer beat a reigning world champion under standard tournament controls.
questions.source: IBM, Deep Blue, https://www.ibm.com/history/deep-blue

questions.q: Who won the first Deep Blue versus Kasparov match in Philadelphia in February 1996?
questions.explain: Kasparov won the 1996 match 4 to 2. Deep Blue did win Game 1, the first win by a computer over a reigning world champion under regular time controls.
questions.source: IBM, Deep Blue, https://www.ibm.com/history/deep-blue

questions.q: According to IBM, how many chess positions per second could Deep Blue evaluate?
questions.explain: IBM states that Deep Blue could evaluate 200 million chess positions per second. It used 32 processors working in parallel.
questions.source: IBM, Deep Blue, https://www.ibm.com/history/deep-blue

questions.q: Shakey, developed at SRI from 1966 to 1972, is described as the first robot of what kind?
options: The first robot to walk on two legs
The first robot sold to consumers
The first mobile robot able to perceive and reason about its surroundings
questions.explain: SRI describes Shakey as the first mobile robot with the ability to perceive and reason about its surroundings. It is now housed at the Computer History Museum.
questions.source: SRI International, Shakey the Robot, https://www.sri.com/hoi/shakey-the-robot/

questions.q: Which magazine called SRI's Shakey the "first electronic person" in 1970?
questions.explain: Life magazine used the phrase in 1970. National Geographic also featured Shakey that year.
questions.source: SRI International, Shakey the Robot, https://www.sri.com/hoi/shakey-the-robot/

questions.q: Who were the three authors of the 2012 AlexNet paper, "ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks"?
questions.explain: Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever and Geoffrey Hinton wrote the paper, published at NeurIPS 2012. Their network was trained on GPUs to classify ImageNet images into 1000 classes.
questions.source: NeurIPS Proceedings, ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks, https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2012/hash/c399862d3b9d6b76c8436e924a68c45b-Abstract.html

questions.q: How many parameters did the AlexNet network have, according to its 2012 paper?
questions.explain: The paper states the network has 60 million parameters, with five convolutional layers and a 1000-way softmax output. It was trained on 1.3 million images.
questions.source: NeurIPS Proceedings, ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks, https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2012/hash/c399862d3b9d6b76c8436e924a68c45b-Abstract.html

questions.q: In the 2012 ImageNet challenge, the SuperVision team's best classification entry had a top-5 error of about 15.3 percent. What was the best error from any other team?
questions.explain: SuperVision scored 0.15315 while the next team, ISI, scored 0.26172. SuperVision was the team of Krizhevsky, Sutskever and Hinton.
questions.source: ImageNet, ILSVRC2012 Results, https://image-net.org/challenges/LSVRC/2012/results.html

questions.q: The 2013 word2vec paper reported learning high quality word vectors from a data set of what size in under a day?
questions.explain: Mikolov, Chen, Corrado and Dean reported learning high quality word vectors from a 1.6 billion word data set in less than a day. The paper introduced two efficient architectures for word embeddings.
questions.source: arXiv, Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space, https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.3781

questions.q: Who was the lead author of the 2014 paper that introduced generative adversarial networks (GANs)?
questions.explain: Ian Goodfellow led the paper, submitted in June 2014, with Yoshua Bengio among the coauthors. It trains a generator and a discriminator against each other.
questions.source: arXiv, Generative Adversarial Networks, https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.2661

questions.q: How many layers deep were the residual networks evaluated in the 2015 ResNet paper?
questions.explain: Kaiming He and colleagues evaluated residual nets with up to 152 layers and reached 3.57 percent error on the ImageNet test set. The work won first place in the ILSVRC 2015 classification task.
questions.source: arXiv, Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition, https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03385

questions.q: What was AlphaGo's result against European champion Fan Hui in October 2015?
questions.explain: AlphaGo beat the three-time European champion 5 to 0. It was the first match between an AI system and a professional Go player.
questions.source: Google DeepMind, AlphaGo, https://deepmind.google/research/breakthroughs/alphago/

questions.q: In what year did the market for specialized Lisp machines collapse?
questions.explain: The Lisp machine market collapsed in 1987 as workstations from companies such as Sun Microsystems offered a powerful alternative.
questions.source: Wikipedia, AI winter, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_winter

questions.q: What is the title of the 2017 paper that introduced the Transformer architecture?
options: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
questions.explain: "Attention Is All You Need" was submitted to arXiv on June 12, 2017. It replaced recurrence and convolutions with attention alone.
questions.source: arXiv, Attention Is All You Need, https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762

questions.q: How many authors are listed on "Attention Is All You Need"?
questions.explain: The paper lists eight authors, from Ashish Vaswani to Illia Polosukhin. Noam Shazeer and Aidan Gomez are among them.
questions.source: arXiv, Attention Is All You Need, https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762

questions.q: What BLEU score did the original Transformer report on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task?
questions.explain: The paper reported 28.4 BLEU on English-to-German. It reported 41.8 BLEU on English-to-French.
questions.source: arXiv, Attention Is All You Need, https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762

questions.q: According to its abstract, how long did the big Transformer train to reach its English-to-French result?
questions.explain: The abstract says the result came after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs. The authors stressed this was a small fraction of the training cost of earlier models.
questions.source: arXiv, Attention Is All You Need, https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762

questions.q: What does the acronym BERT stand for?
questions.explain: BERT stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. Google researchers led by Jacob Devlin submitted the paper in October 2018.
questions.source: arXiv, BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding, https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.04805

questions.q: On how many natural language processing tasks did the BERT paper report new state-of-the-art results?
questions.explain: The BERT abstract reports new state-of-the-art results on eleven NLP tasks. It pushed the GLUE score to 80.5 percent.
questions.source: arXiv, BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding, https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.04805

questions.q: How many parameters did OpenAI's first GPT model (GPT-1, 2018) have?
questions.explain: GPT-1, released in June 2018 with the paper "Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training," had 117 million parameters. It was a twelve-layer decoder-only Transformer.
questions.source: Wikipedia, GPT-1, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-1

questions.q: How many parameters did the full GPT-2 model have?
questions.explain: GPT-2 had 1.5 billion parameters and was trained on about 40 GB of text from 8 million web documents. OpenAI announced it in February 2019.
questions.source: Wikipedia, GPT-2, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-2

questions.q: Why did OpenAI initially withhold the full GPT-2 model in 2019?
options: Licensing disputes over its training data
Concerns about misuse such as spam and fake news
questions.explain: OpenAI cited misuse concerns such as spam and fake news. It released a 774 million parameter version in August 2019 and the full model by November 2019.
questions.source: Wikipedia, GPT-2, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-2

questions.q: How many parameters did GPT-3 have, as stated in its 2020 paper?
questions.explain: The paper describes GPT-3 as a language model with 175 billion parameters, 10 times more than any previous non-sparse language model.
questions.source: arXiv, Language Models are Few-Shot Learners, https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165

questions.q: What was the title of the 2020 paper that introduced GPT-3?
options: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training
questions.explain: GPT-3 was introduced in "Language Models are Few-Shot Learners," submitted May 28, 2020. It showed that scale improves learning from a few examples without fine-tuning.
questions.source: arXiv, Language Models are Few-Shot Learners, https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165

questions.q: In the 2022 InstructGPT paper, outputs from a 1.3 billion parameter InstructGPT model were preferred over outputs from which model?
questions.explain: Labelers preferred the 1.3B InstructGPT outputs to those of the 175B GPT-3 despite 100 times fewer parameters. The model was fine-tuned with reinforcement learning from human feedback.
questions.source: arXiv, Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback, https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155

questions.q: The 2017 paper "Deep reinforcement learning from human preferences" needed human feedback on what share of agent interactions?
questions.explain: Christiano and colleagues reported results while giving feedback on less than one percent of the agent's interactions. They tested on Atari games and simulated robot locomotion.
questions.source: arXiv, Deep reinforcement learning from human preferences, https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03741

questions.q: On what date did OpenAI launch ChatGPT?
questions.explain: ChatGPT launched on November 30, 2022. It initially ran on a GPT-3.5 model.
questions.source: Wikipedia, ChatGPT, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChatGPT

questions.q: How quickly did ChatGPT reach one million users after launch, as reported?
questions.explain: ChatGPT gained one million users in five days and reached 100 million in two months. It was then described as the fastest-growing internet application.
questions.source: Wikipedia, ChatGPT, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChatGPT

questions.q: Which model family did ChatGPT run on when it launched in November 2022?
questions.explain: ChatGPT first ran on GPT-3.5, released alongside the service in November 2022. GPT-4 followed in March 2023.
questions.source: Wikipedia, ChatGPT, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChatGPT

questions.q: According to the GPT-4 Technical Report, what kinds of input could GPT-4 accept?
questions.explain: OpenAI described GPT-4 as a large-scale multimodal model that accepts image and text inputs and produces text outputs. The report was submitted in March 2023.
questions.source: arXiv, GPT-4 Technical Report, https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.08774

questions.q: What did the GPT-4 Technical Report disclose about the model's size?
options: Nothing, the report gave no details on model size
questions.explain: The report states that it contains no further details about the architecture, model size, hardware or training compute. OpenAI cited competition and safety as reasons.
questions.source: arXiv, GPT-4 Technical Report, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2303.08774v6

questions.q: When Anthropic introduced Claude on March 14, 2023, what was the name of the lighter, faster version offered alongside it?
questions.explain: Anthropic offered Claude and Claude Instant, a lighter, less expensive and faster option. Early partners named included Notion, Quora and DuckDuckGo.
questions.source: Anthropic, Introducing Claude, https://www.anthropic.com/news/introducing-claude

questions.q: What context window did Anthropic announce for Claude 2.1 in November 2023?
questions.explain: Claude 2.1 offered a 200,000 token context window, about 150,000 words or over 500 pages. Anthropic also reported a 2x decrease in false statements versus Claude 2.0.
questions.source: Anthropic, Introducing Claude 2.1, https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-2-1

questions.q: What were the three models of the Claude 3 family, announced March 4, 2024?
questions.explain: The Claude 3 family comprised Haiku, Sonnet and Opus in ascending order of capability. All three launched with a 200K token context window.
questions.source: Anthropic, Introducing the next generation of Claude, https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-family

questions.q: What were the three sizes of Google's Gemini 1.0, announced December 6, 2023?
questions.explain: Gemini 1.0 came in Ultra, Pro and Nano sizes. Nano was aimed at on-device tasks.
questions.source: Google, Introducing Gemini: our largest and most capable AI model, https://blog.google/technology/ai/google-gemini-ai/

questions.q: In February 2024 Google said Gemini 1.5 Pro had been successfully tested in research with contexts of up to how many tokens?
questions.explain: Gemini 1.5 Pro shipped with 128,000 tokens as standard and up to 1 million in a limited preview. Google said it had tested up to 10 million tokens in research.
questions.source: Google, Our next-generation model: Gemini 1.5, https://blog.google/technology/ai/google-gemini-next-generation-model-february-2024/

questions.q: Which architecture did Google say Gemini 1.5 used?
questions.explain: Google said Gemini 1.5 uses a Mixture-of-Experts design, in which smaller expert networks are activated selectively depending on the input. It performed at a level broadly similar to 1.0 Ultra.
questions.source: Google, Our next-generation model: Gemini 1.5, https://blog.google/technology/ai/google-gemini-next-generation-model-february-2024/

questions.q: When Meta released LLaMA on February 24, 2023, what was its largest model size?
questions.explain: LLaMA came in 7B, 13B, 33B and 65B sizes under a noncommercial research license. The 33B and 65B models were trained on 1.4 trillion tokens.
questions.source: Meta AI, Introducing LLaMA: A foundational, 65-billion-parameter large language model, https://ai.meta.com/blog/large-language-model-llama-meta-ai/

questions.q: Which company did Meta name as its preferred partner when it introduced Llama 2 in July 2023?
questions.explain: Meta and Microsoft jointly announced Llama 2 on July 18, 2023, with Microsoft as the preferred partner. Unlike the first LLaMA, it was available for commercial use.
questions.source: Meta, Meta and Microsoft Introduce the Next Generation of Llama, https://about.fb.com/news/2023/07/llama-2/

questions.q: How many parameters did Meta's largest Llama 3.1 model have at its July 2024 release?
questions.explain: Llama 3.1 405B was released on July 23, 2024 with a 128,000 token context length. Meta called it the largest openly available foundation model at the time.
questions.source: Meta AI, Introducing Llama 3.1, https://ai.meta.com/blog/meta-llama-3-1/

questions.q: The 2020 paper "Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models" found that loss scales with model size, data size and compute according to what kind of relationship?
questions.explain: Jared Kaplan and colleagues found power-law relationships, some spanning more than seven orders of magnitude. They also found that width and depth mattered little within the ranges tested.
questions.source: arXiv, Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models, https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.08361

questions.q: DeepMind's 2022 Chinchilla paper concluded that for compute-optimal training, model size and training tokens should be scaled how?
options: Model size much faster than tokens
Tokens only, holding model size fixed
Model size only, holding tokens fixed
questions.explain: The paper found that model size and training tokens should be scaled equally, so doubling the model means doubling the tokens. The 70B Chinchilla outperformed the 280B Gopher.
questions.source: arXiv, Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models, https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15556

questions.q: Anthropic's 2022 Constitutional AI method trains with reinforcement learning from what kind of feedback?
questions.explain: Constitutional AI uses RLAIF, reinforcement learning from AI feedback. The only human oversight is a list of rules or principles.
questions.source: arXiv, Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback, https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.08073

questions.q: What dataset did Google's 2019 T5 paper introduce?
options: C4, the Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus
questions.explain: The T5 paper introduced the Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus (C4). It framed every text problem as text-to-text.
questions.source: arXiv, Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer, https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.10683

questions.q: How many TPU v4 chips did Google use to train the 540 billion parameter PaLM model?
questions.explain: PaLM was trained on 6,144 TPU v4 chips using the Pathways system. The paper was submitted in April 2022.
questions.source: arXiv, PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways, https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.02311

questions.q: The 2020 paper that introduced the Vision Transformer (ViT) is titled "An Image is Worth" what?
questions.explain: The title is "An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale." It applied a Transformer directly to sequences of image patches.
questions.source: arXiv, An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale, https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.11929

questions.q: Under what license was Mistral 7B released in 2023?
questions.explain: Mistral 7B was released under the Apache 2.0 license. Its paper says it outperforms Llama 2 13B across all evaluated benchmarks.
questions.source: arXiv, Mistral 7B, https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06825

questions.q: The January 2025 DeepSeek-R1 paper argued that reasoning ability in LLMs can be incentivized through what?
questions.explain: The paper states that reasoning can be incentivized through pure reinforcement learning, without human-labeled reasoning trajectories. It was submitted on January 22, 2025.
questions.source: arXiv, DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning, https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.12948

questions.q: Which two attention techniques does the Mistral 7B paper describe?
options: Grouped-query attention and sliding window attention
questions.explain: Mistral 7B uses grouped-query attention for faster inference and sliding window attention for long sequences at lower cost.
questions.source: arXiv, Mistral 7B, https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06825

questions.q: Who shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics for discoveries that enable machine learning with artificial neural networks?
questions.explain: The prize went to John Hopfield of Princeton and Geoffrey Hinton of the University of Toronto. The citation honors foundational discoveries and inventions that enable machine learning with artificial neural networks.
questions.source: NobelPrize.org, Press release: The Nobel Prize in Physics 2024, https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2024/press-release/

questions.q: According to the Nobel committee, Geoffrey Hinton built on the Hopfield network to create which network?
questions.explain: The press release says Hinton used the Hopfield network as the foundation for the Boltzmann machine, using tools from statistical physics. It can learn characteristic elements in data.
questions.source: NobelPrize.org, Press release: The Nobel Prize in Physics 2024, https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2024/press-release/

questions.q: David Baker received half of the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for what work?
questions.explain: Baker of the University of Washington was honored for computational protein design. The other half went jointly to Demis Hassabis and John Jumper for protein structure prediction.
questions.source: NobelPrize.org, Press release: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2024, https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2024/press-release/

questions.q: In what year did Demis Hassabis and John Jumper present AlphaFold2, according to the 2024 Nobel announcement?
questions.explain: The Nobel announcement says Hassabis and Jumper presented AlphaFold2 in 2020. With it they predicted the structure of virtually all of the 200 million proteins researchers have identified.
questions.source: NobelPrize.org, Press release: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2024, https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2024/press-release/

questions.q: According to the 2024 Nobel Chemistry press release, AlphaFold2 had been used by more than two million people from how many countries?
questions.explain: The press release says AlphaFold2 had been used by more than two million people from 190 countries. Uses cited were antibiotic resistance and enzymes that break down plastic.
questions.source: NobelPrize.org, Press release: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2024, https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2024/press-release/

questions.q: In what year did David Baker design a new protein unlike any other known protein, as cited by the Nobel committee?
questions.explain: The committee says that in 2003 Baker used amino acids to design a new protein unlike any other. The protein is known as Top7.
questions.source: NobelPrize.org, Press release: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2024, https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2024/press-release/

questions.q: Who received the 2018 ACM Turing Award for breakthroughs that made deep neural networks a critical part of computing?
questions.explain: Yoshua Bengio, Geoffrey Hinton and Yann LeCun shared the 2018 Turing Award. The citation cites conceptual and engineering breakthroughs in deep neural networks.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Turing Award, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turing_Award

questions.q: Andrew Barto and Richard Sutton received the 2024 Turing Award for foundations of which field?
questions.explain: Barto and Sutton were honored for developing the conceptual and algorithmic foundations of reinforcement learning.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Turing Award, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turing_Award

questions.q: Who received the 1969 Turing Award for his central role in creating and shaping the field of artificial intelligence?
questions.explain: Marvin Minsky received the 1969 award, and John McCarthy received the award in 1971.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Turing Award, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turing_Award

questions.q: Which pair shared the 1994 Turing Award for pioneering large-scale artificial intelligence systems?
questions.explain: Feigenbaum and Reddy were honored for pioneering the design and construction of large scale AI systems.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Turing Award, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turing_Award

questions.q: Judea Pearl's 2011 Turing Award recognized a calculus for what kind of reasoning?
questions.explain: Pearl was honored for fundamental contributions to AI through a calculus for probabilistic and causal reasoning.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Turing Award, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turing_Award

questions.q: What is the prize amount of the ACM Turing Award, which Google has sponsored since 2014?
questions.explain: The Turing Award carries a prize of US$1 million, funded by Google since 2014. It was first awarded in 1966.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Turing Award, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turing_Award

questions.q: What median Global Distance Test (GDT) score did AlphaFold achieve at the CASP14 assessment in 2020?
questions.explain: AlphaFold scored a median 92.4 GDT, above the roughly 90 GDT level considered competitive with experimental methods. The average error was about 1.6 angstroms.
questions.source: Google DeepMind, AlphaFold: a solution to a 50-year-old grand challenge in biology, https://deepmind.google/discover/blog/alphafold-a-solution-to-a-50-year-old-grand-challenge-in-biology/

questions.q: In what year did the CASP protein structure prediction assessment begin?
questions.explain: CASP began in 1994. AlphaFold's CASP14 result in 2020 was described as a solution to a 50-year-old grand challenge.
questions.source: Google DeepMind, AlphaFold: a solution to a 50-year-old grand challenge in biology, https://deepmind.google/discover/blog/alphafold-a-solution-to-a-50-year-old-grand-challenge-in-biology/

questions.q: Which institute runs the public AlphaFold Protein Structure Database with Google DeepMind?
questions.explain: The database is a partnership between Google DeepMind and EMBL-EBI, the European Bioinformatics Institute. Its data is released under a CC-BY-4.0 license.
questions.source: EMBL-EBI, AlphaFold Protein Structure Database, https://www.alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/

questions.q: On what date did the EU AI Act enter into force?
questions.explain: The AI Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, entered into force on 1 August 2024. Its obligations apply in stages after that date.
questions.source: European Commission, AI Act: Regulatory framework for AI, https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai

questions.q: From what date did the EU AI Act's bans on prohibited AI practices and its AI literacy obligations apply?
questions.explain: The prohibitions and AI literacy obligations applied from 2 February 2025, six months after entry into force.
questions.source: European Commission, AI Act: Regulatory framework for AI, https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai

questions.q: From what date did the EU AI Act's obligations for general-purpose AI models apply?
questions.explain: Obligations for general-purpose AI models applied from 2 August 2025. The European Commission lists this as one of the staged dates after entry into force.
questions.source: European Commission, AI Act: Regulatory framework for AI, https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai

questions.q: What is the official regulation number of the EU AI Act?
questions.explain: The AI Act is Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. Regulation (EU) 2016/679 is the GDPR.
questions.source: European Commission, AI Act: Regulatory framework for AI, https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai

questions.q: How many risk levels does the EU AI Act framework define?
questions.explain: The framework defines four levels: unacceptable risk, high risk, transparency risk and minimal or no risk. Most AI systems in use in the EU fall in the minimal category.
questions.source: European Commission, AI Act: Regulatory framework for AI, https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai

questions.q: According to OpenAI's GPT-4 Technical Report, roughly what percentile did GPT-4 reach on a simulated Uniform Bar Exam?
questions.explain: GPT-4 scored 298 out of 400, about the 90th percentile, on a simulated Uniform Bar Exam. GPT-3.5 scored 213, about the 10th percentile.
questions.source: arXiv, GPT-4 Technical Report, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2303.08774v6

questions.q: What LSAT score did OpenAI report for GPT-4 in its technical report?
questions.explain: OpenAI reported an LSAT score of 163, about the 88th percentile. GPT-3.5 scored 149, about the 40th percentile.
questions.source: arXiv, GPT-4 Technical Report, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2303.08774v6

questions.q: What Codeforces rating did OpenAI report for GPT-4 in its technical report?
questions.explain: OpenAI reported a Codeforces rating of 392 for GPT-4, below the 5th percentile. GPT-3.5 was rated 260, also below the 5th percentile.
questions.source: arXiv, GPT-4 Technical Report, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2303.08774v6

questions.q: What did OpenAI report as GPT-4's score on the GRE Verbal section?
questions.explain: GPT-4 scored 169 out of 170 on GRE Verbal, about the 99th percentile. Its GRE Quantitative score was 163, about the 80th percentile.
questions.source: arXiv, GPT-4 Technical Report, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2303.08774v6

questions.q: On translated versions of the MMLU benchmark, in how many of 26 languages did GPT-4 surpass the previous English-language state of the art?
questions.explain: The GPT-4 Technical Report says GPT-4 surpassed the English-language state of the art in 24 of 26 languages considered. The questions were translated with Azure Translate.
questions.source: arXiv, GPT-4 Technical Report, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2303.08774v6

questions.q: Which two champions did IBM Watson face on Jeopardy! in February 2011?
questions.explain: Watson played Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter, the show's two foremost champions, over three days. IBM donated Watson's winnings to charity.
questions.source: IBM, Watson, Jeopardy! champion, https://www.ibm.com/history/watson-jeopardy

questions.q: In the first Final Jeopardy! round of its 2011 match, Watson gave a low-confidence wrong answer naming which city?
questions.explain: Watson answered "What is Toronto?????" when the correct answer was Chicago. The question marks showed its low confidence.
questions.source: IBM, Watson, Jeopardy! champion, https://www.ibm.com/history/watson-jeopardy

questions.q: Where did AlphaGo play its March 2016 match against Lee Sedol, and what was the result?
questions.explain: AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol 4 to 1 in Seoul in March 2016. DeepMind says the match drew over 200 million viewers.
questions.source: Google DeepMind, AlphaGo, https://deepmind.google/research/breakthroughs/alphago/

questions.q: AlphaGo's famous Move 37 against Lee Sedol had what estimated probability of being played?
questions.explain: DeepMind says Move 37 in game two had a 1 in 10,000 probability of being selected. Lee Sedol later said the move changed his view of AlphaGo.
questions.source: Google DeepMind, AlphaGo, https://deepmind.google/research/breakthroughs/alphago/

questions.q: How many points out of 42 did an advanced version of Gemini with Deep Think score at the 2025 International Mathematical Olympiad?
questions.explain: It solved five of six problems for 35 points, a gold-medal standard confirmed by the IMO. It worked end to end in natural language within the 4.5-hour time limit.
questions.source: Google DeepMind, Advanced version of Gemini with Deep Think officially achieves gold-medal standard at the International Mathematical Olympiad, https://deepmind.google/discover/blog/advanced-version-of-gemini-with-deep-think-officially-achieves-gold-medal-standard-at-the-international-mathematical-olympiad/

questions.q: What standard did Google DeepMind's systems reach at the 2024 International Mathematical Olympiad, the year before Gemini's gold?
questions.explain: In 2024 the systems reached silver-medal standard with 28 points, solving four problems. That approach needed problems translated into formal languages such as Lean and took two to three days of computation.
questions.source: Google DeepMind, Advanced version of Gemini with Deep Think officially achieves gold-medal standard at the International Mathematical Olympiad, https://deepmind.google/discover/blog/advanced-version-of-gemini-with-deep-think-officially-achieves-gold-medal-standard-at-the-international-mathematical-olympiad/

questions.q: Which vehicle won the 2005 DARPA Grand Challenge for autonomous vehicles?
questions.explain: Stanford's Stanley won on October 8, 2005, finishing the 212 km desert course in 6 hours 54 minutes. The prize was $2 million.
questions.source: Wikipedia, DARPA Grand Challenge (2005), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DARPA_Grand_Challenge_(2005)

questions.q: The Bletchley Declaration on AI safety was agreed at a summit held on which dates?
questions.explain: Countries attending the AI Safety Summit agreed the Bletchley Declaration on 1 to 2 November 2023. It focused on the risks of frontier AI.
questions.source: GOV.UK, The Bletchley Declaration by Countries Attending the AI Safety Summit, 1 to 2 November 2023, https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ai-safety-summit-2023-the-bletchley-declaration/the-bletchley-declaration-by-countries-attending-the-ai-safety-summit-1-2-november-2023

questions.q: In what month and year did Geoffrey Hinton announce his resignation from Google, saying he wanted to speak out about AI risks?
questions.explain: Hinton announced his resignation from Google in May 2023 so he could speak out about the risks of AI. He shared the Nobel Prize in Physics the following year.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Geoffrey Hinton, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoffrey_Hinton

questions.q: What MMLU score did Google report for Gemini Ultra in December 2023, calling it the first model to outperform human experts on that test?
questions.explain: Google reported a score of 90.0 percent on MMLU, which covers 57 subjects. It said Gemini Ultra was the first model to outperform human experts on the benchmark.
questions.source: Google, Introducing Gemini: our largest and most capable AI model, https://blog.google/technology/ai/google-gemini-ai/

questions.q: According to the 2024 AI Index, roughly how much compute did OpenAI's GPT-4 use to train, by the report's estimate?
questions.explain: The Stanford AI Index 2024 estimated that GPT-4 used about $78 million worth of compute to train. The figure is an estimate of compute cost, not total development cost.
questions.source: Stanford HAI, AI Index Report 2024, https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2024-ai-index-report

questions.q: The 2024 AI Index estimated the compute cost of training Google's Gemini Ultra at about how much?
questions.explain: The 2024 AI Index estimated that Gemini Ultra cost $191 million in compute to train. The figure covers compute only.
questions.source: Stanford HAI, AI Index Report 2024, https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2024-ai-index-report

questions.q: According to the 2024 AI Index, how much private funding did generative AI attract in 2023?
questions.explain: The 2024 AI Index reported that funding for generative AI reached $25.2 billion in 2023, nearly eight times the 2022 level.
questions.source: Stanford HAI, AI Index Report 2024, https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2024-ai-index-report

questions.q: By roughly what multiple did generative AI funding grow from 2022 to 2023, according to the 2024 AI Index?
questions.explain: The 2024 AI Index said generative AI funding increased nearly eightfold from 2022, reaching $25.2 billion in 2023.
questions.source: Stanford HAI, AI Index Report 2024, https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2024-ai-index-report

questions.q: According to the 2025 AI Index, how much did U.S. private AI investment reach in 2024?
questions.explain: The 2025 AI Index reported U.S. private AI investment of $109.1 billion in 2024, nearly 12 times China's $9.3 billion.
questions.source: Stanford HAI, AI Index Report 2025: Economy, https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report/economy

questions.q: The 2025 AI Index put China's 2024 private AI investment at how much?
questions.explain: The 2025 AI Index reported China's private AI investment at $9.3 billion in 2024, compared with $109.1 billion in the United States and $4.5 billion in the United Kingdom.
questions.source: Stanford HAI, AI Index Report 2025, https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report

questions.q: According to the 2025 AI Index, how much private investment did generative AI attract globally in 2024?
questions.explain: The 2025 AI Index reported $33.9 billion in global private investment in generative AI in 2024, up 18.7 percent from 2023.
questions.source: Stanford HAI, AI Index Report 2025, https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report

questions.q: The 2025 AI Index reported total corporate AI investment in 2024 of about how much?
questions.explain: The 2025 AI Index said corporate AI investment reached $252.3 billion in 2024, with private investment rising 44.5 percent.
questions.source: Stanford HAI, AI Index Report 2025: Economy, https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report/economy

questions.q: What share of survey respondents reported AI use by their organizations in 2024, according to the 2025 AI Index?
questions.explain: The 2025 AI Index reported that 78 percent of respondents said their organizations used AI in 2024, up from 55 percent the year before.
questions.source: Stanford HAI, AI Index Report 2025: Economy, https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report/economy

questions.q: According to the 2025 AI Index, how did reported business use of generative AI change from 2023 to 2024?
questions.explain: The 2025 AI Index reported that generative AI business use more than doubled, from 33 percent in 2023 to 71 percent in 2024.
questions.source: Stanford HAI, AI Index Report 2025: Economy, https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report/economy

questions.q: Among organizations using AI in service operations, what did most report about cost savings, according to the 2025 AI Index?
questions.explain: The 2025 AI Index found that 49 percent of respondents using AI in service operations reported cost savings, and most of them reported savings of less than 10 percent.
questions.source: Stanford HAI, AI Index Report 2025: Economy, https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report/economy

questions.q: The 2025 AI Index reported that AI inference cost fell by more than how much between November 2022 and October 2024?
questions.explain: The 2025 AI Index reported that inference cost fell from $20.00 to $0.07 per million tokens over that period, a more than 280-fold reduction in about 18 months.
questions.source: Stanford HAI, AI Index Report 2025: Research and Development, https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report/research-and-development

questions.q: According to the 2025 AI Index, by about how much per year have machine learning hardware costs been dropping?
questions.explain: The 2025 AI Index reported that hardware price performance improved with costs dropping 30 percent per year, while energy efficiency improved 40 percent annually.
questions.source: Stanford HAI, AI Index Report 2025: Research and Development, https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report/research-and-development

questions.q: The 2025 AI Index estimated the training carbon emissions of GPT-4 at about how many tons?
questions.explain: The 2025 AI Index listed estimated training emissions of 588 tons for GPT-3, 5,184 tons for GPT-4 and 8,930 tons for Llama 3.1 405B.
questions.source: Stanford HAI, AI Index Report 2025: Research and Development, https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report/research-and-development

questions.q: According to the 2025 AI Index, about what share of notable AI models in 2024 came from industry?
questions.explain: The 2025 AI Index reported that nearly 90 percent of notable models in 2024 came from industry, up from 60 percent in 2023.
questions.source: Stanford HAI, AI Index Report 2025: Research and Development, https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report/research-and-development

questions.q: In 2023, how many notable machine learning models did industry produce, according to the 2024 AI Index?
questions.explain: The 2024 AI Index counted 51 notable models from industry in 2023, compared with 15 from academia and 21 from industry and academia collaborations.
questions.source: Stanford HAI, AI Index Report 2024, https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2024-ai-index-report

questions.q: According to the 2025 AI Index, roughly how often does training compute for notable AI models double?
questions.explain: The 2025 AI Index reported that training compute for notable AI models is doubling approximately every five months.
questions.source: Stanford HAI, AI Index Report 2025: Research and Development, https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report/research-and-development

questions.q: Epoch AI estimated in May 2024 that the compute used to train notable and frontier models grew by roughly what factor per year from 2010 to May 2024?
questions.explain: Epoch AI reported that the compute used to train recent models grew 4 to 5 times per year from 2010 to May 2024.
questions.source: Epoch AI, Training compute of frontier AI models grows by 4 to 5x per year, https://epoch.ai/blog/training-compute-of-frontier-ai-models-grows-by-4-5x-per-year

questions.q: Epoch AI estimated in June 2024 that the cost of the largest training runs has grown by about what factor per year since 2016?
questions.explain: Epoch AI estimated training costs for frontier models have grown about 2.4 times per year since 2016.
questions.source: Epoch AI, How much does it cost to train frontier AI models?, https://epoch.ai/blog/how-much-does-it-cost-to-train-frontier-ai-models

questions.q: By what year did Epoch AI project, in June 2024, that the largest training runs would cost more than a billion dollars?
questions.explain: Epoch AI projected that, if the trend continued, the largest training runs would cost more than a billion dollars by 2027.
questions.source: Epoch AI, How much does it cost to train frontier AI models?, https://epoch.ai/blog/how-much-does-it-cost-to-train-frontier-ai-models

questions.q: What did Nvidia report as its full-year Data Center revenue for fiscal 2024?
questions.explain: In its fiscal 2024 results, Nvidia reported record full-year Data Center revenue of $47.5 billion, up 217 percent.
questions.source: NVIDIA, NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2024, https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2024

questions.q: By what percentage did Nvidia say its Data Center revenue rose in fiscal 2024?
questions.explain: Nvidia reported that full-year Data Center revenue rose 217 percent to $47.5 billion in fiscal 2024.
questions.source: NVIDIA, NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2024, https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2024

questions.q: What full-year Data Center revenue did Nvidia report for fiscal 2025?
questions.explain: Nvidia reported fiscal 2025 Data Center revenue of a record $115.2 billion, up 142 percent from a year earlier.
questions.source: NVIDIA, NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2025, https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025

questions.q: What total revenue did Nvidia report for fiscal 2025?
questions.explain: Nvidia reported fiscal 2025 revenue of $130.5 billion, up 114 percent from a year earlier.
questions.source: NVIDIA, NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2025, https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025

questions.q: In January 2023, how did Microsoft describe the new investment it announced in OpenAI?
questions.explain: On January 23, 2023, Microsoft announced a multiyear, multibillion dollar investment in OpenAI as the third phase of their partnership. Microsoft did not state an exact amount in that announcement.
questions.source: Microsoft, Microsoft and OpenAI extend partnership, https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2023/01/23/microsoftandopenaiextendpartnership/

questions.q: In its January 2023 announcement, what role did Microsoft say Azure would play for OpenAI?
options: One of three equal cloud suppliers
A backup provider for research only
questions.explain: Microsoft said Azure would remain OpenAI's exclusive cloud provider, powering OpenAI workloads across research, products and API services.
questions.source: Microsoft, Microsoft and OpenAI extend partnership, https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2023/01/23/microsoftandopenaiextendpartnership/

questions.q: Microsoft's January 2023 announcement described the new OpenAI deal as which phase of the partnership, following investments in which years?
options: The first phase, with no prior investment
questions.explain: Microsoft called the January 2023 agreement the third phase of its partnership with OpenAI, following its previous investments in 2019 and 2021.
questions.source: Microsoft, Microsoft and OpenAI extend partnership, https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2023/01/23/microsoftandopenaiextendpartnership/

questions.q: In January 2024, the IMF estimated that almost what share of global employment is exposed to AI?
questions.explain: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva wrote that almost 40 percent of global employment is exposed to AI, based on IMF staff analysis.
questions.source: International Monetary Fund, AI Will Transform the Global Economy. Let's Make Sure It Benefits Humanity, https://www.imf.org/en/Blogs/Articles/2024/01/14/ai-will-transform-the-global-economy-lets-make-sure-it-benefits-humanity

questions.q: According to the IMF's January 2024 analysis, about what share of jobs in advanced economies may be impacted by AI?
questions.explain: The IMF estimated that about 60 percent of jobs in advanced economies may be impacted by AI, and that roughly half of those exposed jobs may benefit from AI integration.
questions.source: International Monetary Fund, AI Will Transform the Global Economy. Let's Make Sure It Benefits Humanity, https://www.imf.org/en/Blogs/Articles/2024/01/14/ai-will-transform-the-global-economy-lets-make-sure-it-benefits-humanity

questions.q: What AI exposure did the IMF estimate for low-income countries in January 2024?
questions.explain: The IMF estimated AI exposure of 40 percent in emerging markets and 26 percent in low-income countries, compared with about 60 percent in advanced economies.
questions.source: International Monetary Fund, AI Will Transform the Global Economy. Let's Make Sure It Benefits Humanity, https://www.imf.org/en/Blogs/Articles/2024/01/14/ai-will-transform-the-global-economy-lets-make-sure-it-benefits-humanity

questions.q: Which three countries posted the highest scores on the IMF's AI Preparedness Index, as reported in January 2024?
options: Singapore, the United States and Denmark
questions.explain: The IMF said Singapore, the United States and Denmark posted the highest scores on its AI Preparedness Index.
questions.source: International Monetary Fund, AI Will Transform the Global Economy. Let's Make Sure It Benefits Humanity, https://www.imf.org/en/Blogs/Articles/2024/01/14/ai-will-transform-the-global-economy-lets-make-sure-it-benefits-humanity

questions.q: In the NBER version of 'The Simple Macroeconomics of AI', Daron Acemoglu estimated AI would raise total factor productivity by no more than how much over 10 years?
questions.explain: Acemoglu's NBER working paper estimated no more than a 0.66 percent increase in total factor productivity over 10 years, a far smaller figure than many industry forecasts.
questions.source: NBER, The Simple Macroeconomics of AI (Working Paper 32487), https://www.nber.org/papers/w32487

questions.q: After accounting for hard-to-learn tasks, what did Acemoglu's NBER paper predict for TFP gains over the next 10 years?
questions.explain: Acemoglu argued that early evidence comes from easy-to-learn tasks, so he predicted TFP gains over 10 years would be even more modest, less than 0.53 percent.
questions.source: NBER, The Simple Macroeconomics of AI (Working Paper 32487), https://www.nber.org/papers/w32487

questions.q: In the April 2024 draft of 'The Simple Macroeconomics of AI', what share of U.S. labor tasks did Acemoglu calculate to be exposed to AI?
questions.explain: Using Eloundou et al.'s exposure estimates weighted by wage bill, Acemoglu's April 2024 draft calculated that 19.9 percent of U.S. labor tasks are exposed to AI.
questions.source: MIT Economics, The Simple Macroeconomics of AI (April 2024 draft), https://economics.mit.edu/sites/default/files/2024-04/The%20Simple%20Macroeconomics%20of%20AI.pdf

questions.q: In Acemoglu's April 2024 draft, what share of AI-exposed tasks did he assume could be profitably performed by AI, based on Svanberg et al.?
questions.explain: Acemoglu used Svanberg et al.'s estimate that among exposed tasks, 23 percent can be profitably performed by AI, with costs exceeding benefits for the rest.
questions.source: MIT Economics, The Simple Macroeconomics of AI (April 2024 draft), https://economics.mit.edu/sites/default/files/2024-04/The%20Simple%20Macroeconomics%20of%20AI.pdf

questions.q: In March 2023, Goldman Sachs economists estimated that generative AI could expose the equivalent of how many full-time jobs to automation?
questions.explain: Goldman Sachs economists Joseph Briggs and Devesh Kodnani wrote that shifts in workflows could expose the equivalent of 300 million full-time jobs to automation.
questions.source: Goldman Sachs, Generative AI could raise global GDP by 7%, https://www.goldmansachs.com/insights/articles/generative-ai-could-raise-global-gdp-by-7-percent

questions.q: Goldman Sachs Research said in 2023 that generative AI could drive what increase in global GDP over a 10-year period?
questions.explain: Goldman Sachs Research said generative AI could drive a 7 percent, or almost $7 trillion, increase in global GDP and lift productivity growth by 1.5 percentage points over 10 years.
questions.source: Goldman Sachs, Generative AI could raise global GDP by 7%, https://www.goldmansachs.com/insights/articles/generative-ai-could-raise-global-gdp-by-7-percent

questions.q: Goldman Sachs economists estimated in 2023 that roughly what share of U.S. occupations are exposed to some degree of automation by AI?
questions.explain: Analyzing the task content of over 900 occupations, Goldman Sachs economists estimated that roughly two-thirds of U.S. occupations are exposed to some degree of automation by AI.
questions.source: Goldman Sachs, Generative AI could raise global GDP by 7%, https://www.goldmansachs.com/insights/articles/generative-ai-could-raise-global-gdp-by-7-percent

questions.q: According to a Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory report released by the U.S. Department of Energy in December 2024, about what share of total U.S. electricity did data centers consume in 2023?
questions.explain: The DOE said data centers consumed about 4.4 percent of total U.S. electricity in 2023 and could consume about 6.7 to 12 percent by 2028.
questions.source: U.S. Department of Energy, DOE Releases New Report Evaluating Increase in Electricity Demand from Data Centers, https://www.energy.gov/articles/doe-releases-new-report-evaluating-increase-electricity-demand-data-centers

questions.q: The December 2024 LBNL report for the U.S. Department of Energy estimated U.S. data center electricity use at how much in 2023?
questions.explain: The DOE said U.S. data center electricity use rose from 58 TWh in 2014 to 176 TWh in 2023, with projections of 325 to 580 TWh by 2028.
questions.source: U.S. Department of Energy, DOE Releases New Report Evaluating Increase in Electricity Demand from Data Centers, https://www.energy.gov/articles/doe-releases-new-report-evaluating-increase-electricity-demand-data-centers

questions.q: In what year did the Luddite movement begin?
questions.explain: The Luddite movement began in Arnold, Nottinghamshire, on 11 March 1811, and spread through England over the following two years.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Luddite, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luddite

questions.q: In which English county did the Luddite movement begin?
questions.explain: The movement began in Arnold, Nottinghamshire, and spread rapidly through England over the following two years.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Luddite, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luddite

questions.q: The name 'Luddite' is traced to which figure?
options: Edward Lud, a Member of Parliament who opposed mills
Ludwig Lutter, a German loom inventor
Lord Ludlow, a mill owner in Yorkshire
Ned Ludd, an apprentice said to have smashed two stocking frames
questions.explain: The term derives from Ned Ludd, an apocryphal apprentice who allegedly smashed two stocking frames in 1779.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Luddite, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luddite

questions.q: How did Parliament respond to machine breaking in 1812?
options: It set a national minimum wage for weavers
It granted the Luddites a royal pardon
It made machine breaking a capital crime
questions.explain: The Destruction of Stocking Frames, etc. Act 1812 made machine breaking a capital crime.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Luddite, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luddite

questions.q: About how many government troops were involved in suppressing Luddite activity?
questions.explain: About 12,000 government troops, most of them from militia or yeomanry units, were involved in suppressing Luddite activity.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Luddite, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luddite

questions.q: In which 1930 essay did John Maynard Keynes warn of a 'new disease' called technological unemployment?
options: The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money
The Economic Consequences of the Peace
questions.explain: Keynes used the phrase technological unemployment in his 1930 essay Economic Possibilities for our Grandchildren.
questions.source: Yale Department of Economics (course reprint), John Maynard Keynes, Economic Possibilities for our Grandchildren (1930), http://www.econ.yale.edu/smith/econ116a/keynes1.pdf

questions.q: How did Keynes define technological unemployment in 1930?
options: Unemployment caused by workers refusing to learn new machines
Unemployment from finding ways to economise on labour faster than new uses for labour can be found
Unemployment caused by a shortage of capital for factories
Unemployment caused by imports of foreign machinery
questions.explain: Keynes described it as unemployment due to our discovery of means of economising the use of labour outrunning the pace at which we can find new uses for labour, and called it a temporary phase of maladjustment.
questions.source: Yale Department of Economics (course reprint), John Maynard Keynes, Economic Possibilities for our Grandchildren (1930), http://www.econ.yale.edu/smith/econ116a/keynes1.pdf

questions.q: Keynes predicted in 1930 that the standard of life in progressive countries a hundred years later would be how much higher?
options: Between four and eight times as high
Between twenty and thirty times as high
questions.explain: Keynes predicted that the standard of life in progressive countries one hundred years hence would be between four and eight times as high as in 1930.
questions.source: Yale Department of Economics (course reprint), John Maynard Keynes, Economic Possibilities for our Grandchildren (1930), http://www.econ.yale.edu/smith/econ116a/keynes1.pdf

questions.q: What working week did Keynes suggest in 1930 might spread the remaining work as widely as possible?
questions.explain: Keynes wrote that three-hour shifts or a fifteen-hour week may put off the problem for a great while.
questions.source: Yale Department of Economics (course reprint), John Maynard Keynes, Economic Possibilities for our Grandchildren (1930), http://www.econ.yale.edu/smith/econ116a/keynes1.pdf

questions.q: In their 2013 study, Frey and Osborne estimated that about what share of total U.S. employment was at high risk of computerisation?
questions.explain: Frey and Osborne estimated that about 47 percent of total U.S. employment is at risk of computerisation. The estimate concerns technical risk, not a forecast of actual job losses.
questions.source: Oxford Martin School, The Future of Employment: How Susceptible Are Jobs to Computerisation?, https://www.oxfordmartin.ox.ac.uk/publications/the-future-of-employment

questions.q: How many detailed occupations did Frey and Osborne analyze in 'The Future of Employment'?
questions.explain: Frey and Osborne examined 702 detailed occupations, using a Gaussian process classifier to estimate each one's probability of computerisation.
questions.source: Oxford Martin School, The Future of Employment: How Susceptible Are Jobs to Computerisation?, https://www.oxfordmartin.ox.ac.uk/publications/the-future-of-employment

questions.q: What relationship did Frey and Osborne find between wages, educational attainment and an occupation's probability of computerisation?
options: A positive relationship for wages only
questions.explain: Frey and Osborne found that wages and educational attainment exhibit a strong negative relationship with an occupation's probability of computerisation.
questions.source: Oxford Martin School, The Future of Employment: How Susceptible Are Jobs to Computerisation?, https://www.oxfordmartin.ox.ac.uk/publications/the-future-of-employment

questions.q: In 'GPTs are GPTs' (2023), Eloundou and coauthors estimated that about 80% of the U.S. workforce could have at least what share of their tasks affected by large language models?
questions.explain: The paper estimated that about 80 percent of the U.S. workforce could have at least 10 percent of their work tasks affected by the introduction of LLMs.
questions.source: arXiv, GPTs are GPTs: An Early Look at the Labor Market Impact Potential of Large Language Models, https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.10130

questions.q: In 'GPTs are GPTs', about what share of U.S. workers might see at least half of their tasks affected by LLMs?
questions.explain: Eloundou and coauthors estimated that about 19 percent of workers may see at least 50 percent of their tasks impacted.
questions.source: arXiv, GPTs are GPTs: An Early Look at the Labor Market Impact Potential of Large Language Models, https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.10130

questions.q: According to 'GPTs are GPTs', what share of all U.S. worker tasks could be completed faster at the same quality with access to an LLM alone?
questions.explain: The paper estimated about 15 percent of tasks could be completed faster at the same quality with an LLM alone, rising to between 47 and 56 percent with software built on top of LLMs.
questions.source: arXiv, GPTs are GPTs: An Early Look at the Labor Market Impact Potential of Large Language Models, https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.10130

questions.q: In 'Generative AI at Work', Brynjolfsson, Li and Raymond found that access to an AI assistant raised customer support productivity by how much on average?
questions.explain: The study found that access to the tool increased productivity, measured by issues resolved per hour, by 14 percent on average.
questions.source: NBER, Generative AI at Work (Working Paper 31161), https://www.nber.org/papers/w31161

questions.q: In 'Generative AI at Work', which workers saw the largest productivity gain from the AI assistant?
options: Novice and low-skilled workers, with a 34% improvement
Experienced and highly skilled workers, with a 34% improvement
All workers equally, with a 14% improvement
questions.explain: The authors found a 34 percent improvement for novice and low-skilled workers and minimal impact on experienced and highly skilled workers.
questions.source: NBER, Generative AI at Work (Working Paper 31161), https://www.nber.org/papers/w31161

questions.q: How many customer support agents did the 'Generative AI at Work' study draw data from?
questions.explain: Brynjolfsson, Li and Raymond studied the staggered introduction of a generative AI assistant using data from 5,179 customer support agents.
questions.source: NBER, Generative AI at Work (Working Paper 31161), https://www.nber.org/papers/w31161

questions.q: The WEF Future of Jobs Report 2025 projected how many new jobs would be created from 2025 to 2030?
questions.explain: The WEF projected the creation of new jobs equivalent to 14 percent of current total employment, or 170 million jobs, between 2025 and 2030.
questions.source: World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025, https://reports.weforum.org/docs/WEF_Future_of_Jobs_Report_2025.pdf

questions.q: How many current jobs did the WEF Future of Jobs Report 2025 expect to be displaced by 2030?
questions.explain: The WEF expected displacement of the equivalent of 8 percent, or 92 million, of current jobs over 2025 to 2030.
questions.source: World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025, https://reports.weforum.org/docs/WEF_Future_of_Jobs_Report_2025.pdf

questions.q: What net employment change did the WEF Future of Jobs Report 2025 project for 2025 to 2030?
questions.explain: Combining 170 million jobs created and 92 million displaced, the WEF projected net growth of 7 percent of total employment, or 78 million jobs.
questions.source: World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025, https://reports.weforum.org/docs/WEF_Future_of_Jobs_Report_2025.pdf

questions.q: According to the WEF Future of Jobs Report 2025, what share of workers' existing skill sets are expected to be transformed or become outdated over 2025 to 2030?
questions.explain: The WEF said workers can expect 39 percent of their existing skill sets to be transformed or outdated, down from 44 percent in 2023 and 57 percent in 2020.
questions.source: World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025, https://reports.weforum.org/docs/WEF_Future_of_Jobs_Report_2025.pdf

questions.q: What share of employers in the WEF Future of Jobs Report 2025 anticipated reducing their workforce where AI can automate tasks?
questions.explain: The WEF reported that half of employers plan to reorient their business in response to AI, while 40 percent anticipate reducing their workforce where AI can automate tasks.
questions.source: World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025, https://reports.weforum.org/docs/WEF_Future_of_Jobs_Report_2025.pdf

questions.q: Which roles did the WEF Future of Jobs Report 2025 list among the fastest declining?
options: Postal service clerks, bank tellers and data entry clerks
Farmworkers, delivery drivers and construction workers
Big data specialists and fintech engineers
questions.explain: The WEF said businesses expect the fastest declining roles to include postal service clerks, bank tellers and data entry clerks.
questions.source: World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025, https://reports.weforum.org/docs/WEF_Future_of_Jobs_Report_2025.pdf

questions.q: Which roles did the WEF Future of Jobs Report 2025 expect to see the largest growth in absolute numbers?
options: Frontline roles such as farmworkers and delivery drivers
questions.explain: The WEF predicted frontline roles, such as farmworkers, delivery drivers, construction workers and salespersons, would grow the most in absolute terms, while technology roles grow fastest in percentage terms.
questions.source: World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025, https://reports.weforum.org/docs/WEF_Future_of_Jobs_Report_2025.pdf

questions.q: If the world's workforce were 100 people, how many would need training by 2030, according to the WEF Future of Jobs Report 2025?
questions.explain: The WEF estimated 59 of every 100 workers would need training by 2030, and that 11 of them would be unlikely to receive it.
questions.source: World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025, https://reports.weforum.org/docs/WEF_Future_of_Jobs_Report_2025.pdf

questions.q: In February 2024, Klarna said its AI assistant was doing the equivalent work of how many full-time agents?
questions.explain: Klarna said its AI assistant, live for one month, was doing the equivalent work of 700 full-time agents. This is the company's own claim.
questions.source: Klarna, Klarna AI assistant handles two-thirds of customer service chats in its first month, https://www.klarna.com/international/press/klarna-ai-assistant-handles-two-thirds-of-customer-service-chats-in-its-first-month/

questions.q: What share of its customer service chats did Klarna say its AI assistant handled in its first month?
questions.explain: Klarna said the assistant had 2.3 million conversations in its first month, two-thirds of its customer service chats.
questions.source: Klarna, Klarna AI assistant handles two-thirds of customer service chats in its first month, https://www.klarna.com/international/press/klarna-ai-assistant-handles-two-thirds-of-customer-service-chats-in-its-first-month/

questions.q: How did Klarna say average errand resolution time changed after its AI assistant launched in 2024?
options: From 11 minutes to less than 2 minutes
questions.explain: Klarna said customers resolved errands in less than 2 minutes, compared with 11 minutes previously.
questions.source: Klarna, Klarna AI assistant handles two-thirds of customer service chats in its first month, https://www.klarna.com/international/press/klarna-ai-assistant-handles-two-thirds-of-customer-service-chats-in-its-first-month/

questions.q: How much profit improvement did Klarna estimate its AI assistant would drive in 2024?
questions.explain: Klarna said the assistant was estimated to drive a $40 million profit improvement in 2024. This was a company estimate made one month after launch.
questions.source: Klarna, Klarna AI assistant handles two-thirds of customer service chats in its first month, https://www.klarna.com/international/press/klarna-ai-assistant-handles-two-thirds-of-customer-service-chats-in-its-first-month/

questions.q: Under the 2023 WGA agreement summary, what can AI not do with literary material?
options: Be used by writers in any form
questions.explain: The WGA summary states that AI can't write or rewrite literary material, and AI-generated material will not be considered source material under the MBA.
questions.source: Writers Guild of America, Summary of the 2023 WGA MBA, https://www.wgacontract2023.org/the-campaign/summary-of-the-2023-wga-mba

questions.q: Under the 2023 WGA agreement, can a company require a writer to use AI software such as ChatGPT?
options: No, though a writer may choose to use AI with company consent
Yes, but only on streaming projects
No, and writers are barred from using AI at all
questions.explain: The WGA summary says a writer can choose to use AI if the company consents, but the company can't require the writer to use AI software.
questions.source: Writers Guild of America, Summary of the 2023 WGA MBA, https://www.wgacontract2023.org/the-campaign/summary-of-the-2023-wga-mba

questions.q: What disclosure does the 2023 WGA agreement require from companies regarding AI?
options: They must publish all AI training data
They must report AI use to the Copyright Office
They must tell writers if materials given to them were generated by AI
They must label every episode that used AI
questions.explain: The WGA summary says the company must disclose to the writer if any materials given to the writer have been generated by AI or incorporate AI-generated material.
questions.source: Writers Guild of America, Summary of the 2023 WGA MBA, https://www.wgacontract2023.org/the-campaign/summary-of-the-2023-wga-mba

questions.q: In James Bessen's 2015 account, what happened to the number of tellers needed per bank branch between 1988 and 2004 as ATMs spread?
questions.explain: Bessen wrote that the number of tellers required to operate a branch fell from 20 to 13 between 1988 and 2004, yet teller jobs did not decline because banks opened more branches.
questions.source: IMF Finance & Development, Toil and Technology (James Bessen, March 2015), https://www.imf.org/external/pubs/ft/fandd/2015/03/bessen.htm

questions.q: According to Bessen, how did banks respond as ATMs cut the cost of running a branch?
options: Banks moved tellers into ATM repair
questions.explain: Bessen reported that bank branches in urban areas increased 43 percent over the period, offsetting fewer tellers per branch.
questions.source: IMF Finance & Development, Toil and Technology (James Bessen, March 2015), https://www.imf.org/external/pubs/ft/fandd/2015/03/bessen.htm

questions.q: Autor, Chin, Salomons and Seegmiller found that the majority of current U.S. employment is in job specialties introduced after which year?
questions.explain: Their study of new job titles from 1940 to 2018 found that the majority of current employment is in new job specialties introduced after 1940.
questions.source: NBER, New Frontiers: The Origins and Content of New Work, 1940 to 2018 (Working Paper 30389), https://www.nber.org/papers/w30389

questions.q: According to Autor and coauthors, where has new work creation shifted since 1980?
options: Toward middle-paid production and clerical occupations
Toward high-paid professional and, secondarily, low-paid service occupations
