questions.explain: They found new work shifted from middle-paid production and clerical occupations over 1940 to 1980 to high-paid professional and, secondarily, low-paid services since 1980.
questions.source: NBER, New Frontiers: The Origins and Content of New Work, 1940 to 2018 (Working Paper 30389), https://www.nber.org/papers/w30389

questions.q: The 2,080-hour full-time work year is based on what assumption, according to OPM?
questions.explain: OPM notes the older 2,080-hour figure assumed 52 weeks of 40-hour workweeks, or 364 days. Federal agencies now use a 2,087-hour divisor to reflect the average calendar year.
questions.source: U.S. Office of Personnel Management, Computing Hourly Rates of Pay Using the 2,087-Hour Divisor, https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/pay-administration/fact-sheets/computing-hourly-rates-of-pay-using-the-2087-hour-divisor/

questions.q: What hour divisor does OPM use to compute federal hourly pay, reflecting the average work hours in a year over a 28-year cycle?
questions.explain: OPM uses a 2,087-hour divisor, the average number of work hours in a calendar year over a 28-year cycle, in place of the 2,080 hours used before 1984.
questions.source: U.S. Office of Personnel Management, Computing Hourly Rates of Pay Using the 2,087-Hour Divisor, https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/pay-administration/fact-sheets/computing-hourly-rates-of-pay-using-the-2087-hour-divisor/

questions.q: Under the BLS Current Population Survey, how many hours per week must someone usually work to be counted as full time?
questions.explain: BLS defines full-time workers as those who usually work 35 or more hours per week, and part-time workers as those who usually work fewer than 35.
questions.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Labor Force Statistics (CPS) Concepts and Definitions, https://www.bls.gov/cps/definitions.htm

questions.q: Under the federal WARN Act, how much advance written notice must a covered employer give before a plant closing or mass layoff?
questions.explain: The Department of Labor says WARN requires at least 60 calendar days advance written notice of a covered plant closing or mass layoff.
questions.source: U.S. Department of Labor, Plant Closings and Layoffs, https://www.dol.gov/general/topic/termination/plantclosings

questions.q: The WARN Act generally applies to employers with how many employees?
questions.explain: The Department of Labor says WARN applies to employers with 100 or more employees.
questions.source: U.S. Department of Labor, Plant Closings and Layoffs, https://www.dol.gov/general/topic/termination/plantclosings

questions.q: According to Challenger, Gray & Christmas, how many U.S. job cuts announced in May 2023 were attributed to AI, the first month it broke out that reason?
questions.explain: Challenger reported that 3,900 of the 80,089 job cuts announced in May 2023 were attributed to AI, marking its first time breaking out cuts based on that factor.
questions.source: Challenger, Gray & Christmas, May 2023 Layoffs Jump on Tech, Retail, Auto; YTD Hiring Lowest Since 2016, https://www.challengergray.com/blog/may-2023-layoffs-jump-on-tech-retail-auto-ytd-hiring-lowest-since-2016/

questions.q: Under the WARN Act, which reduction counts as a mass layoff at a single site during a 30-day period?
options: Any layoff of 10 or more employees
At least 100 employees regardless of site size
At least 500 employees, or at least 50 who make up at least 33% of employees
questions.explain: Under 29 U.S.C. 2101, a mass layoff is a reduction in force that causes employment loss for at least 500 employees, or for at least 50 employees who are at least 33 percent of the workforce, at a single site during any 30-day period.
questions.source: Cornell Law School LII, 29 U.S. Code § 2101: Definitions; exclusions from definition of loss of employment, https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/29/2101

questions.q: Under the WARN Act, a plant closing is covered when a shutdown causes employment loss for how many employees at a single site during a 30-day period?
questions.explain: 29 U.S.C. 2101 defines a plant closing as a shutdown of a single site, or units within it, that results in employment loss for 50 or more employees during any 30-day period.
questions.source: Cornell Law School LII, 29 U.S. Code § 2101: Definitions; exclusions from definition of loss of employment, https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/29/2101

questions.q: Which of these does NOT count as an 'employment loss' under the WARN Act?
options: A termination other than for cause
A cut of more than 50% in hours each month for 6 months
questions.explain: WARN defines employment loss as a termination other than a discharge for cause, voluntary departure or retirement; a layoff exceeding 6 months; or a reduction in hours of more than 50 percent during each month of a 6-month period.
questions.source: Cornell Law School LII, 29 U.S. Code § 2101: Definitions; exclusions from definition of loss of employment, https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/29/2101

questions.q: Under the WARN Act, who counts as a part-time employee excluded from the headcount thresholds?
options: Someone working fewer than 35 hours a week
Someone averaging fewer than 20 hours a week, or employed fewer than 6 of the prior 12 months
questions.explain: 29 U.S.C. 2101 defines a part-time employee as one employed for an average of fewer than 20 hours per week or for fewer than 6 of the 12 months before notice is required.
questions.source: Cornell Law School LII, 29 U.S. Code § 2101: Definitions; exclusions from definition of loss of employment, https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/29/2101

questions.q: Besides affected workers or their representative, who must receive a WARN notice?
options: The state dislocated worker unit and the chief elected local official
questions.explain: 29 U.S.C. 2102 requires notice to affected employees or their representative, the state's rapid response unit, and the chief elected official of the local government.
questions.source: Cornell Law School LII, 29 U.S. Code § 2102: Notice required before plant closings and mass layoffs, https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/29/2102

questions.q: Which circumstance can allow an employer to give less than 60 days of WARN notice?
options: A decision to adopt AI tools
Business circumstances that were not reasonably foreseeable
A desire to keep the layoff confidential
A layoff announced in a press release
questions.explain: 29 U.S.C. 2102 allows reduced notice for a faltering company, unforeseeable business circumstances, or natural disaster, but the employer must give as much notice as is practicable.
questions.source: Cornell Law School LII, 29 U.S. Code § 2102: Notice required before plant closings and mass layoffs, https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/29/2102

questions.q: If an employer violates the WARN Act, back pay to each affected employee is capped at how many days?
questions.explain: Under 29 U.S.C. 2104, an employer is liable for back pay for each day of violation up to a maximum of 60 days, and never more than half the days the employee was employed.
questions.source: Cornell Law School LII, 29 U.S. Code § 2104: Administration and enforcement of requirements, https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/29/2104

questions.q: In the JOLTS survey, how does BLS classify an employee who leaves a job voluntarily?
questions.explain: BLS defines quits as employees who left voluntarily, separate from layoffs and discharges, which are involuntary separations initiated by the employer.
questions.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, JOLTS Definitions, https://www.bls.gov/jlt/jltdef.htm

questions.q: In the JOLTS survey, retirements are counted under which category of separations?
questions.explain: BLS classifies retirements, transfers to other locations, deaths and separations due to disability as other separations, distinct from quits and layoffs.
questions.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, JOLTS Definitions, https://www.bls.gov/jlt/jltdef.htm

questions.q: How does Challenger, Gray & Christmas count job cuts in its monthly report?
options: As announced plans by U.S.-based employers
questions.explain: Challenger reports job cuts announced by U.S.-based employers, which are stated plans and may differ from the number of terminations that actually occur.
questions.source: Challenger, Gray & Christmas, May 2023 Layoffs Jump on Tech, Retail, Auto; YTD Hiring Lowest Since 2016, https://www.challengergray.com/blog/may-2023-layoffs-jump-on-tech-retail-auto-ytd-hiring-lowest-since-2016/

questions.q: As of its June 2026 report, how many job cut announcements had Challenger, Gray & Christmas attributed to AI since it began tracking AI as a distinct reason in 2023?
questions.explain: Challenger said that since 2023, when AI was first tracked as a distinct reason, it had been cited in 173,568 job cut announcements through June 2026.
questions.source: Challenger, Gray & Christmas, Challenger Report: June Layoffs Cool to 45,849, Down 53% from May; AI Leads Reasons for Fourth Consecutive Month, https://www.challengergray.com/blog/challenger-report-june-layoffs-cool-to-45849-down-53-from-may-ai-leads-reasons-for-fourth-consecutive-month/

questions.q: In the BLS displaced worker survey, which workers are counted as long-tenured displaced workers?
options: Any worker who quit in the past year
Workers who had held their jobs 3 or more years and lost them to a closing, slack work or abolished position
questions.explain: BLS counts displaced workers as people 20 and older who lost or left jobs because their plant or company closed or moved, there was insufficient work, or their position or shift was abolished, and focuses on those with 3 or more years of tenure.
questions.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Worker Displacement news release, https://www.bls.gov/news.release/disp.nr0.htm

questions.q: Under BLS definitions, does a person on temporary layoff need to be searching for work to be counted as unemployed?
options: No, if they expect to be recalled
Yes, at least once a week
They are never counted as unemployed
questions.explain: BLS counts people temporarily laid off and expecting recall as unemployed, without requiring an active job search.
questions.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Labor Force Statistics (CPS) Concepts and Definitions, https://www.bls.gov/cps/definitions.htm

questions.q: On Daily AI Toll, what does the 'direct' causality label mean?
options: AI was one of several factors
The company explicitly states AI or automation as the primary reason for the cuts
Cuts occurred in AI-exposed roles without any statement
questions.explain: The methodology labels an event direct when the company explicitly states AI or automation as the primary reason for the cuts.
questions.source: Daily AI Toll, Methodology, https://dailyaitoll.com/methodology

questions.q: Why does Daily AI Toll describe its totals as a lower bound?
options: The site rounds every number down to the nearest thousand
Many AI-related job losses go unreported or are attributed to other factors
questions.explain: The methodology says the data is a lower bound estimate because many AI-related losses go unreported, are attributed to other factors, or are not disclosed by companies.
questions.source: Daily AI Toll, Methodology, https://dailyaitoll.com/methodology

questions.q: Which of these does Daily AI Toll's methodology say it does not track?
options: Cuts where the company names AI as the main reason
Cuts where AI was one of several factors
questions.explain: The methodology excludes general layoffs without an AI connection, hiring pauses and attrition, contractor reductions, job transformations and forecasts.
questions.source: Daily AI Toll, Methodology, https://dailyaitoll.com/methodology

questions.q: Below what confidence score are events typically excluded from Daily AI Toll?
questions.explain: Each event gets a confidence score from 0.0 to 1.0, and events below 0.4 are typically excluded.
questions.source: Daily AI Toll, Methodology, https://dailyaitoll.com/methodology

questions.q: Why can a high task exposure estimate, such as Goldman Sachs's 2023 figures, not be read directly as a count of layoffs?
options: Exposure estimates count only jobs already eliminated
Exposure measures tasks that could be automated, and Goldman said not all automated work will translate into layoffs
Exposure figures are published only after layoffs occur
questions.explain: Goldman Sachs estimated that exposed occupations could see a quarter to as much as half of their workload replaced, but said not all automated work will translate into layoffs.
questions.source: Goldman Sachs, Generative AI could raise global GDP by 7%, https://www.goldmansachs.com/insights/articles/generative-ai-could-raise-global-gdp-by-7-percent
